title: Article 326 — Elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assemblies of States to be on the basis of adult suffrage

content.overview: Article 326 provides that elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage; that is to say, every person who is a citizen of India and who is not less than eighteen years of age on such date as may be fixed in that behalf by or under any law made by the appropriate Legislature and is not otherwise disqualified under the Constitution or any law on the ground of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice, shall be entitled to be registered as a voter at any such election.
content.glance: Adult suffrage for Lok Sabha and State Assemblies: citizen + age ≥18 + not disqualified (non-residence, unsound mind, crime, corrupt/illegal practice).
content.study:
Article 326 adult suffrage:
- Applies to elections to the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies.
- Voter: citizen of India; not less than 18 years (reduced from 21 by the 61st Amendment); not disqualified under the Constitution or law on grounds of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime, or corrupt or illegal practice.
- Detailed qualifications/disqualifications are in the Representation of the People Acts and related law.

Examination: adult suffrage; 18 years; citizen; listed disqualification grounds; 61st Amendment.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections on the basis of adult suffrage.
2. Entitled to registration as voter: citizen; age ≥18 on the prescribed date; not disqualified on grounds of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime, or corrupt or illegal practice.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is adult suffrage under Article 326?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 326, elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage. Every person who is a citizen of India, is not less than eighteen years of age on the date fixed by or under law, and is not otherwise disqualified under the Constitution or any law on the ground of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice, shall be entitled to be registered as a voter at any such election.
